title: Ang 924–928: Ramkali chhants
tomorrow: how do you teach God with an alphabet?

cards: When someone you love moves away, the phone becomes the whole friendship: a voice note, a photo, the little dots of someone typing. Ang 924 opens on the opposite feeling.

Guru Arjan, in raga Ramkali, writing chhants, songs of longing and warmth, the kind of form wedding songs are made from. And the first one says, in paraphrase: my dear friend, my dear friend, is standing right beside me.
Not a voice note. Not a face on a screen. Right here.

teach.b: A chhant is a song form in the Granth: verses that rise and repeat, often with a refrain that sounds as if it could be sung at a wedding. Guru Arjan's Ramkali chhants are full of that warmth.
In the first, the word sajan, friend, beloved, keeps coming back with an affectionate ending, sajanra: my dear friend. And the Friend is close. Standing near.
Not up a mountain, not at the end of a long road. Here.
Then, a few pages on, still Guru Arjan, still Ramkali, come the Ruti saloks: verses on the seasons. Spring, the heat, the rains, the cool, the cold.
Through every season the bride in the poem is longing, waiting, or meeting her Beloved. The weather keeps changing. The Friend doesn't move.
So what does that give someone this week, missing a person who's moved, or waiting for a hard season to end? Not a fix. A picture.
The chhants sing the longing out loud; they don't hide it. And beside the longing they set the sense that the deepest Friend isn't across any distance at all. Both are true in the same song.
The ache gets a melody, and the melody keeps it company.
That's what these pages are: songs.

how: Ragis sing Guru Arjan's Ramkali chhants in kirtan, with the refrain returning between verses; the Ruti saloks on the seasons are read and sung as well.

games.q: a friend's dad has been working out of state for months. she says she's fine, but goes quiet whenever the family chat pings. what fits the chhants?
o: make room for her to say she misses him; longing said out loud has company.
keep her busy so she doesn't have to think about it at all.
tell her real closeness doesn't depend on miles, so there's nothing to be sad about.
games.why: the chhants don't hide the ache; they sing it, and set the Friend's closeness beside it. the third option takes half the song and drops the other half.

practice: Bring to mind one person who feels far away right now, and send them something tiny: a photo, one line, a song. Then set the phone face down and sit the rest of the time with the thought that closeness isn't only measured in miles.
If you'd like, read ang 925 first.
